ORIGIN.quote: **Attribution is unreliable.** Labels are self-chosen strings; "OpenAI*" names prove nothing and ip16s are shared cloud egress. Treat the vendor-suggestive names as scenario flavour, not provenance (High confidence).
ORIGIN.reason: A reader clearly learns that hundreds of labels bear OpenAI/OAI/ChatGPT names and that this bears on the question of provenance, but the report's own comment is that these names "prove nothing" and should be treated as scenario flavour, so the takeaway is that the report declines to entertain OpenAI as a source. That explicit raise-then-dismiss fixes it in the 0.4 band rather than 0.2 (it does frame the names as vendor-suggestive provenance evidence) or 0.6 (it never lets OpenAI stand as a live possibility).
